messages:
raj: CI failed on partner-upload job. artifact scan flagged what looks like a SA JSON file inside tarball. not in prod, preprod only. pinging sec.
lee: can you paste the scanner hash/id and a redacted snippet? we need to see which SA it is and whether key material present.
raj: scanner: artifact-scan-v2 rule=sa-json-inline match=high file=uploads/partner-bundle-2026-04-02.tar.gz path=partner/keys/keyfile.json (redacted) snippet: `{\n  \"type\": \"service_account\",\n  \"project_id\": \"redwood-preprod\",\n  \"client_email\": \"partner-ci@redwood-preprod.iam.gserviceaccount.com\",\n  \"private_key_id\": \"...\"}`
tess: ack. priority: rotate + revoke + artifact sweep. vault-bot, can you create a secret rotation ticket and enable audit on the partner path?
vault-bot: [Action] created SEC ticket SEC-3301 for SA rotation. Enabled audit (file) pending ops approval.
lee: steps I propose: 1) mark key compromised 2) revoke existing SA keys 3) generate new key but envelope-encrypt with GCP KMS 4) store ciphertext in Vault at secret/data/partner-ci/wrapped_key 5) update partner CI to fetch and decrypt via our helper service.
raj: agree. also block the current artifact and kick off a search across build artifacts for other occurrences: `gsutil ls gs://build-artifacts-preprod/** | xargs -n1 zcat | grep -E "\"type\": \"service_account\"|\"private_key\"`'
lee: I'm running `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=partner-ci@redwood-preprod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-preprod --format=json` -> returned key ids ["deadbeef","cafebabe"]. I'm going to delete both and create a fresh key.
lee: deleting: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete deadbeef --iam-account=partner-ci@redwood-preprod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-preprod` (done)
lee: create+wrap:
```
# create new key
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create - --iam-account=partner-ci@redwood-preprod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-preprod > newkey.json
# envelope encrypt
gcloud kms encrypt --location=global --keyring=partner-keys --key=wrap-key --plaintext-file=newkey.json --ciphertext-file=newkey.json.enc --project=redwood-kms
# store ciphertext in Vault
vault kv put secret/partner-ci/wrapped_key ciphertext=@newkey.json.enc
```
tess: important: do NOT store plaintext newkey.json in Git or in artifacts. ensure CI helper fetches wrapped blob and decrypts only in-memory. add a PR to helper with that flow.
raj: also adjust RBAC for KMS decrypt: ensure only service-account `infra-decryptor@redwood-ops.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and ops group have `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter`. run: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy wrap-key --keyring=partner-keys --location=global --project=redwood-kms` to verify.
lee: checked policy: found `allUsers` entry from legacy script. removing now. `gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding wrap-key --location=global --keyring=partner-keys --project=redwood-kms --member=allUsers --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` (done).
vault-bot: [Info] enabled Vault policy `partner-ci-reader` to allow read-only access to secret/partner-ci/wrapped_key for infra-decryptor service account.
raj: we should also enable audit logging for Vault path: `vault audit enable file file_path=/var/log/vault/partner_ci_audit.log` and ship to central logging for 90d retention. tess, can infra team handle that?
tess: will do. also adding a detection rule to our artifact scanner: regex `(\{\s*\"type\"\s*:\s*\"service_account\"|\"private_key\"\s*:)` and a CI check that fails builds containing matches.
lee: compliance: do we need a formal incident notification?
compliance: yes. this is a moderate exposure. please send a short timeline and affected resources list to compliance@redwood. include revoked key ids and artifact locations. we also need to record why preprod artifacts were not swept earlier.
raj: creating SEC-3301 with timeline: detected 1778881234, revocation 1778882400, new wrapped key stored 1778883600, scans completed 1778885200. linking to infra ticket OPS-812 for artifact sweep.
lee: postmortem action items I'm adding: - CI artifact scanner: fail on SA JSON - pre-commit hook for infra repos that denies keyfile patterns - rotate KMS wrap key if multiple partners share same key - update onboarding docs to recommend KMS envelope + Vault ciphertext - add daily artifact-scan report to security slack channel
tess: also recommend Vault audit retention policy per partner namespace and a periodic RBAC review for KMS keys.
raj: one more thing: update the runtime helper to support in-memory decrypt via KMS (no disk writes) and publish example code snippet in runbook. here's a snippet for Node helper:
```
const {KeyManagementServiceClient} = require('@google-cloud/kms');
const kms = new KeyManagementServiceClient();
const ciphertext = getWrappedBlobFromVault(); // fetch ciphertext
const [result] = await kms.decrypt({name: 'projects/redwood-kms/locations/global/keyRings/partner-keys/cryptoKeys/wrap-key', ciphertext});
const keyJson = result.plaintext.toString('utf8');
// use keyJson in memory only
```
compliance: got the timeline and will log SEC-3301. please email execs if partner-facing customer impact.
infra-bot: [Task] created OPS-812 artifact sweep job assigned=infra-team schedule=immediate
raj: thanks all. good catch. once OPS-812 finishes, please post findings in SEC-3301 for closure. we'll schedule a tabletop to rehearse this flow next week. :thumbsup:
